challenge.exploration_summary: I explored the jwt project, a Go JWT library. The project has a Claims interface, RegisteredClaims and MapClaims implementations, a Validator for claims validation, and a Parser with functional options. I noticed that the errors.go file already defines ErrTokenInvalidId but no validation logic uses it. The RegisteredClaims struct has an ID field for the jti claim, but there is no way to validate it through the Validator. The Claims interface doesn't have a GetID method, so I used an optional interface pattern (similar to ClaimsValidator) to add jti validation without breaking the Claims interface.
challenge.feature_spec: JWT ID (jti) Claim Validation: Adds the ability to validate the jti (JWT ID) claim through the Validator. This includes: (1) GetID() method on MapClaims and RegisteredClaims, (2) expectedID field and verifyID method on Validator that uses a type assertion to an optional GetID interface, (3) WithID parser option, and (4) integration into the Validate flow. The feature follows existing patterns for iss/sub validation. When WithID is set, the jti claim is required and must match the expected ID. When not set, jti validation is skipped entirely.
challenge.feature_rationale: The jti (JWT ID) claim is a standard registered claim per RFC 7519 Section 4.1.7 that provides a unique identifier for a token, useful for preventing replay attacks. The library already defines ErrTokenInvalidId and has ID field in RegisteredClaims, but lacks the validation infrastructure. This feature completes the jti support by adding validation in the same style as iss, sub, and aud, using an optional interface approach to maintain backward compatibility with the Claims interface.
challenge.bug_description: The verifyID method in validator.go uses a type assertion to check if claims implement the optional GetID interface. When the type assertion fails (claims don't implement GetID), the original code correctly returns errorIfRequired(required, "jti"), which produces an ErrTokenRequiredClaimMissing error when WithID is set. The bug changes this to return nil, silently skipping jti validation. This means that if a developer configures WithID("expected-id") to prevent replay attacks, but uses a custom claims type that does not implement the GetID method, the jti validation is completely bypassed and tokens without any jti claim are accepted as valid. This is a security vulnerability because it silently defeats the replay protection that the developer explicitly configured.

findings.description: In verifyID(), when the claims object does not implement the optional GetID interface, the function silently returns nil even when required=true (i.e., WithID was set). This means jti validation is bypassed entirely for any custom claims type that doesn't implement GetID, allowing tokens with arbitrary or missing jti claims to pass validation. The fix returns errorIfRequired(required, "jti") instead of nil, so that when WithID is configured and claims lack GetID support, an ErrTokenRequiredClaimMissing error is properly raised.

self_review.fix_explanation: The PR was applied incorrectly, causing code fragments from different files (validator.go, map_claims.go, registered_claims.go, parser_option.go) to be interleaved, which made the codebase uncompilable. I reconstructed all four files from the intended design, preserving the feature while fixing one logic bug: in verifyID(), when claims don't implement the GetID interface and required is true, the original code silently returned nil (bypassing jti validation). I changed it to return errorIfRequired(required, "jti"), which returns ErrTokenRequiredClaimMissing when WithID is set. This follows the same pattern used by verifyIssuer/verifySubject which rely on the mandatory Claims interface methods rather than optional type assertions.
